summary: V36 placed each middle-palm anchor at the solved paddle point but did not prove that the shaft passed inside the fingers. Closed-finger V1 preserves those palm and wrist targets, resolves the real lower-shaft or upper T-grip axis for each hand, and lays the four visible non-thumb finger chains onto a deterministic three-segment arc around that axis. The result reads as a closed hand around the paddle in the retained profile and rear views without the rejected wrist twist or buried upper hand.

accepted: All five production avatars retain the existing two-hand grip while each visible non-thumb distal chain is now positioned around the actual shaft or transverse T-grip axis.

The palm-anchor metric remains within 0.25 cm and the new eight-joint distal-contact metric remains within 0.25 cm for every avatar; the archived roster reports a 1.880034572465661e-9 cm maximum anchor error and 0.0 cm maximum contact error.
The retained guide and broadest-body full, profile and rear views show the lower fingers enclosing the paddle shaft and the upper fingers closing around the T-grip without the rejected wrist twist.
The UE 5.8 editor build and exact-current M4, M5, M7 and M8 suites are green.
rejected_or_open: A full shaft/T-grip hand frame was rejected because it created a twisted-mitten silhouette and an implausible T-grip ring.
Stronger generic curl alone was rejected because it closed the fingers while leaving the grip at the edge of the hand.
A closed-finger cage-centroid translation was rejected because it shifted the wrist by 5.5 to 5.9 cm and buried the upper hand.
A bounded forearm-axis roll plus weighted grip centre was rejected because the shaft still sat beside the visible finger loop.
The deterministic distal-contact metric covers eight non-thumb distal joints; thumb contact remains an authored-curl visual-review item rather than a contact-constrained guarantee.

The procedural production hand mesh, finger proportions, knuckles, skin deformation, wet response and synchronized rafting stroke remain visibly synthetic and below final photoreal character-art approval.
No named guide or character-art reviewer has approved hand placement, grip safety, stroke biomechanics or these captures, and none is approved for release media.
open_gates: A named character-art reviewer must approve or replace the coarse procedural hand anatomy, deformation and material response.
A qualified whitewater guide must approve the two-hand shaft/T-grip placement and stroke biomechanics.
M9 remains blocked by all wider human, platform, signing, media, clean-build, performance and promotion gates.
